m:starom: The square is free. The Orloj «chimes» every hour on the hour from 9am to 11pm (from the city's official website): arrive 10 minutes early to get a spot. You can go up the Town Hall tower for the view, with a separate ticket (price to be checked on the Town Hall website). The «trdelník» isn't a Czech sweet: it comes from elsewhere in Central Europe and is sold mainly to tourists.
m:karlov: The bridge is always open and free: at dawn (before 8am) or at sunset it's much quieter. Watch out for pickpockets in the crush. At the Lennon Wall you can leave a message, but spray-painting graffiti is forbidden.
m:hrad: The main circuit costs 450 crowns (about €18.40) and is valid for 2 days; reduced 300 crowns. The outer castle grounds are open every day from 6am to 10pm; the historic buildings from 9am to 5pm from April to October and from 9am to 4pm from November to March (data from the Castle website, via guides). On Sundays the Cathedral opens at noon because of services: hours can change for state events, check hrad.cz. The changing of the guard is every day at noon in the first courtyard.
m:josef: It's closed on Saturdays and Jewish holidays. The Jewish Museum's hours are normally 9am to 6pm from April to October and 9am to 4:30pm from November to March (Sunday–Friday): I've used the more cautious one. The ticket costs more than €15 (price not read on the website: check jewishmuseum.cz) and the Old-New Synagogue is paid separately.
m:vaclav: The square is a boulevard and free to walk. The National Museum at the top is normally open every day (hours and prices to be checked on nm.cz). The souvenir bazaar and the bars on the boulevard are very touristy: the good places are on the side streets.
m:petrin: The funicular is public transport: the public transport ticket normally covers it (check on the DPP website whether it's running: it sometimes closes for maintenance). Going up the tower is paid separately (a few euros, price to be checked) and hours vary with the season. In good weather it's worth staying until sunset.
m:vysehrad: The fortress and gardens are free and open all day. The basilica and cemetery have a separate ticket or donation (a few euros, hours to be checked). To get back, walk downhill to Vyšehrad metro C station.
m:letna: The park is free and always open. The beer garden (Letenský zámeček and the Beer Garden) is normally open from spring to October, in good weather. From here you can walk back to the Old Town across the Čechův bridge.
m:zizkov: The observation deck is paid (about €15, price not read on the website: check towerpark.cz). Riegrovy sady has a beer garden, open in good weather.
vd:bakeshop: A bakery with a café a short walk from Old Town Square: bread, croissants, sandwiches and Czech baked goods for a quick breakfast, to take away too.
vp:bakeshop: Breakfast around €5–8 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:lokal: A Czech beer hall-tavern in the centre, with freshly tapped beer and traditional dishes: goulash, svíčková, fried cheese. Order at the counter; the tables are long and shared.
vp:lokal: A main course usually costs €8–12 and a beer about €2 (menu not seen). Hours from guides: check before going.
vd:nasemaso: A butcher's with a restaurant where you eat a Czech beef burger or a meat sandwich at the counter: a few things, done well, and honest prices for the centre.
vp:nasemaso: A burger with chips is around €8–12 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:louvre: The historic 1902 café once frequented by Kafka and Einstein: tall rooms with chandeliers, billiards and a simple Czech menu. Breakfast and coffee with a cake are the best moments.
vp:louvre: Breakfast around €8–12 and a dish of the day around €10–14 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:savoy: A neo-Renaissance café in Malá Strana with painted ceilings and its own pâtisserie: big breakfasts, cakes and homemade bread. A few steps from the Petřín funicular.
vp:savoy: Breakfast around €10–14 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:bilek: The Malá Strana beer hall-tavern, a short walk from Charles Bridge: the same style as Lokál, with Czech cooking, tapped Pilsner and long tables.
vp:bilek: A dish is around €8–12 (menu not seen). Hours from guides: check before going.
vd:kantyna: A butcher's canteen in the centre: take a tray and order meat at the counter, cut and cooked to order, with sides and beer. Always full of locals.
vp:kantyna: A meal with meat and a side is around €10–14 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:imperial: An Art Nouveau café-restaurant with walls covered in ceramic tiles and a mosaic ceiling: the place for an elegant breakfast without spending much.
vp:imperial: Breakfast usually costs €10–14 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:kmotra: An underground Czech tavern near the National Theatre, with grandmother's cooking: soups, thin Czech-style pizza and meat dishes with dumplings, at local prices.
vp:kmotra: A dish is around €8–12 (menu not seen). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
cd:staromestska: Take the lift up to the viewpoint next to the Orloj: views over the red roofs and the square.
cd:mucha: Posters, paintings and drawings by Alfons Mucha, the master of Czech Art Nouveau.
cd:comunismo: Life in Czechoslovakia under the regime: reconstructions of schools, shops and offices of the time.
cd:kafka: Manuscripts, letters and installations devoted to the writer, on the bank of the Vltava.
cd:clementinum: The Baroque library with frescoed vaults and the astronomical tower, on a guided tour.
cx:clementinum: Entry only on a guided tour at fixed times.
cd:strahov: Two Baroque halls full of old books and globes, viewed from the doorway.
cd:loreta: A Baroque shrine near the Castle, with a cloister and a treasury of monstrances.
cn:cubismo: House of the Black Madonna, Museum of Cubism
cd:cubismo: Czech Cubist furniture and paintings in a 1912 building.
cd:narodni: The neo-Renaissance building at the top of Wenceslas Square, with the pantheon hall and natural history collections.
cd:vltava: An hour by boat among the bridges, the Castle and the city's palaces.
cd:zoopraga: One of Europe's best zoos, on a hill above the Vltava.
